result.rationale: In refreshOAuthTokens, sharing mode does `const response = await fetch(...); return response;` — a raw fetch Response with no `.data`. The Google CalendarService call site does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` then `token.access_token`, which matches the gaxios shape only returned by the non-sharing branch (`return fetchTokens.res`). In sharing mode `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws, so Google token refresh crashes whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set.

judged_text: In credential-sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this call site reads res?.data — a gaxios-only shape that does not exist on a fetch Response — so token is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError. Every Google token refresh crashes in sharing deployments, so the sync feature breaks the very integration flow it was built for; Google Calendar is unusable whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then does `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` are set. A `fetch` Response has no `.data` property, so `token` will be `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw. This is directly verifiable from the diff and would break Google token refresh in credential-sharing mode.
